name: Governance Authority Structure
consequences: Choosing between absolute hierarchical rule enforced through surveillance, decentralized council-based governance with rotating representation, or hybrid rule-by-consensus with an unelected executive board fundamentally shapes how conflicts are resolved and whether the population views authority as legitimate or coercive. A heavily centralized model will suppress dissent faster but breeds resentment and underground opposition; decentralization slows decision-making but increases buy-in and reduces the risk of catastrophic policy errors cascading through the entire population.
options: Establish an unelected executive council of founding elite stakeholders with full legislative and enforcement authority, supported by pervasive surveillance to eliminate coordinated resistance.
Institute floor-based councils with elected representatives who propose policy but require majority sign-off from a permanent board of technical experts (agriculture, power, water, security).

Rotate governance responsibilities across population cohorts annually, with all major policy decisions requiring supermajority votes from delegated block representatives and a veto power retained only for existential threats.
review: Absolute hierarchy suppresses immediate dissent but invites generational rebellion once surveillance fatigue sets in; rotation-based systems build legitimacy but risk paralysis if floor councils deadlock on life-critical resource allocation.

name: Construction Phasing and Seal Timeline
consequences: The project can be built as a single continuous excavation and sealed once occupancy reaches critical mass (faster time-to-closure, higher initial capital burn), or constructed in modular phases with each section sealed independently and tested before the next begins (lower annual costs, longer total timeline, higher risk of population bottlenecks during early phases). Early sealing locks in architectural decisions and forces rapid population adaptation; phased sealing allows iterative design adjustment but extends the period when the structure remains vulnerable to external interference.
options: Excavate and construct all 144 floors simultaneously across six parallel zones, pour all concrete and install all mechanical systems, then conduct rapid integrated testing and seal the primary entrance within 18 months of foundation-breaking.

Construct Floors 1–36 (residential and agricultural core) as the first module, achieve full operational independence and population stabilization for 3,000 people, seal and test for 12 months, then begin excavation on Floors 37–72 using lessons learned.

Prioritize excavation of the top 48 floors first, seal that section after 18 months to establish a self-proving concept, then use data from early operations to redesign and excavate the lower 96 floors based on observed population dynamics and technical performance.
review: Single-pour construction compresses risk into one catastrophic failure point and forces untested governance into operation immediately; phased sealing creates interim population instability and multiplies seal-related technical challenges but allows design corrections that could prevent irreversible systemic failures.

name: Ecosystem Redundancy and Failure Tolerance
consequences: The silo can rely on single integrated systems (one water recycler, one air filtration plant, one power generation facility) scaled to theoretical maximum capacity with no backup, minimizing construction cost and floor space but eliminating recovery options if a critical system fails. Alternatively, redundant parallel systems can be built into every subsystem (three independent water recyclers, dual air plants, hybrid power from multiple sources), increasing construction cost and consuming valuable floor space but enabling graceful degradation. System failure in a single-backup model triggers rapid population attrition; system failure in a redundant model triggers managed conservation and maintenance protocols.
options: Design all power generation, water recycling, and air filtration as single integrated systems operating at 100% theoretical capacity with no parallel backup, using saved floor space for additional residential or agricultural capacity.

Install three independent power systems (fusion core, kinetic energy storage, geothermal tap) and dual water and air plants, each capable of meeting 60% of demand independently, requiring 20% more excavation but enabling one-system failure survival.

Distribute water, air, and power generation into six micro-systems across different silo sectors, each serving one geographic cluster, so that localized failure affects only 15% of the population and can be manually routed around during repair cycles.
review: Single monolithic systems maximize space efficiency but a single compressor or pump failure kills the entire population within days, whereas distributed micro-systems fragment maintenance expertise and create bottlenecks if multiple sectors require simultaneous repair.

name: Information Control and External Reality Narrative
consequences: The silo's stated rationale for underground existence hinges on believing the surface world is permanently toxic. This can be maintained through complete information lockdown (no outside broadcasts, no window access, no archived pre-silo media), conditional truth (selective news from outside, curated to prove toxicity), or radical transparency (unfiltered external broadcasts and regular surface expeditions). Lockdown maximizes population compliance but risks catastrophic trust collapse if residents discover the narrative is false; transparency erodes control but prevents the destabilizing moment of mass disillusionment if external reality contradicts official doctrine.
options: Prohibit all external media, seal all surface-facing sensors and windows, limit outside knowledge to sanitized briefings delivered by security officials, and classify pre-silo history as irrelevant to current operations.

Allow monitored external broadcasts during designated hours in common areas, with live feeds filtered to remove information suggesting the surface is habitable, and maintain that residents cannot survive outside without specialized suits and decontamination.

Enable residents to access unfiltered external broadcasts in private viewing booths, permit volunteer surface expeditions in full protective gear every two years, and document all external conditions in publicly available logs to establish a continuous empirical record.
review: Total information lockdown collapses the moment a maintenance crew discovers unsealed outside access; selective curation requires permanent censorship resources and fails if external reality contradicts doctrine; unfiltered transparency undermines the legitimacy of underground confinement but prevents a future violent reckoning.

name: Population Growth and Reproduction Policy
consequences: The silo can impose strict birth controls (one child per adult pair, state-assigned reproduction slots) to maintain stable demand for the 144-floor capacity, or encourage reproduction to fill all available space and grow the population to theoretical maximum (5,000–8,000 people), or permit voluntary reproduction with natural equilibrium as population density increases. Strict controls ensure resource predictability but create generational resentment and require enforcement infrastructure; maximum growth accelerates the timeline to self-sustaining operations but multiplies resource strain and creates cascading conflicts over space allocation if demand ever exceeds capacity.
options: Implement mandatory reproductive licensing with centralized assignment of breeding slots to maintain population at exactly 3,500 people, with each license tied to career contribution and social compliance scoring.

Permit all consenting adult pairs to reproduce without restriction, with the understanding that space, food, and water per capita will decline as population grows, creating natural incentives toward lower birth rates as conditions tighten.

Establish a tiered reproductive incentive system where the first two children per pair receive full resource allocations, the third child receives 75% allocation (smaller living space, reduced food rations), and fourth-plus children are not permitted, creating a soft ceiling at roughly 5,000 population.
review: Strict licensing builds compliance surveillance infrastructure and creates a barren generational cohort if enforcement is even briefly interrupted; unrestricted growth risks overshoot that cannot be reversed without starvation rationing; tiered incentives require continuous adjustment as population dynamics shift and create perverse incentives for elite stakeholders to exempt themselves.

name: Elite Stakeholder Separation and Privileges
consequences: Private investors and government officials who funded the silo can be segregated into exclusive upper-floor residential zones with superior resources, climate control, and privacy (strengthening their commitment to the project but creating a visible caste system that breeds resentment among the general population), integrated into the general population with no special privileges (increasing fairness but risking that elite stakeholders withdraw funding if they face resource constraints), or granted functional leadership positions with proportional resource access tied to ongoing operational responsibilities. Elite separation accelerates early funding confidence; integration maximizes long-term legitimacy; functional integration risks both legitimacy and funding confidence simultaneously.
options: Designate Floors 1–12 as restricted elite residential and administrative zones, with superior life support, 40% larger living quarters, exclusive dining facilities, and exemption from manual labor rotation, funded by founding stakeholder agreements.

Assign all residents, including founding investors and government officials, to the same lottery system for floor assignment and resource allocation, with no preferential access except those elected to governance councils during their service terms.

Create a tiered system where founding stakeholders retain usufruct rights to Floors 1–6 during their lifetime, with those territories reverting to general population housing upon death, and require stakeholder nominees to rotate through operational command roles (agriculture, water, power, security) to earn extended privileges.
review: Permanent elite floors entrench inequality and create an internal two-state system vulnerable to uprising if resentment reaches critical mass; equal lottery assignment risks withdrawing investor confidence if early conditions are uncomfortable; lifetime usufruct with reversion creates incentive misalignment (elites optimize for their lifespan, not intergenerational stability).

name: Surface Reentry Protocol and Exit Capability
consequences: The silo can be designed as a permanent seal with no operable surface exit (maximizing population containment and information control but making the structure a literal tomb if catastrophic internal failure forces evacuation), include a single emergency surface lock usable only by authorized personnel (preserving control while allowing emergency retreat), or maintain multiple operational surface exits with developed external infrastructure (enabling voluntary surface departure, reducing control, but preventing psychological desperation if internal conditions deteriorate). Sealed design locks commitment but eliminates escape; single-lock design preserves option value for elite stakeholders; multiple exits enable population retention only through sustained legitimacy.
options: Seal the primary surface entrance after population settlement, retain only a concealed emergency pressure-relief hatch in the upper levels known only to the security apparatus for catastrophic depressurization relief, with no operable exit for the general population.

Install a single controlled surface airlock on Floor 1 with biometric access limited to security and medical personnel, maintained for emergency evacuation and supply replenishment, but not available for voluntary exit without executive authorization.

Develop three operational surface facilities with separate emergency airlocks, maintain external decontamination structures and supply warehouses, and permit voluntary surface departure after a mandatory 10-year residency period and security screening to establish an operational external migration pathway.
review: Sealed design guarantees internal population retention and prevents elite escape, but mass panic and violence will result from any uncontrolled breach event; single-lock design preserves elite exit while imprisoning general population, creating maximum resentment; multiple exits reduce elite control but may be the only governance model that sustains social stability across generations.

name: Capital Investment Tranching and Default Risk
consequences: How construction funding is released in phases—lump-sum upfront, milestone-based drawdowns, or perpetual revenue-sharing—directly shapes which stakeholders bear cost overruns and abandonment risk. A front-loaded model locks private investors into sunk-cost escalation; milestone-based drawdowns allow exit but risk project stalling if funds are withheld mid-construction.
options: Require all funding as upfront government bonds with private investors taking 20% equity only after foundation completion, shifting early abandonment risk to public treasuries.

Structure as a 30-year revenue-share model where private backers receive returns from silo-internal economies (agriculture, manufacturing, energy) once sealed and operational, deferring their capital at-risk until inhabitant productivity proves viable.

Establish a rotating venture consortium with mandatory quarterly rebalancing, where any stakeholder can exit by transferring their claim to an escrow-held successor fund, preserving liquidity but fragmenting long-term strategic alignment.
review: Upfront government bonds minimize private investor flight but create political vulnerability if the project shows signs of failure; revenue-sharing delays stakeholder confidence and compounds cost inflation through extended construction; quarterly exit clauses preserve flexibility but invite predatory claim transfers and destabilize funding discipline.

name: Vertical Subsystem Integration and Single-Point Failure Topology
consequences: Whether air filtration, water recycling, and power generation are physically layered (all serving the entire 144-floor column) or geographically distributed (each sector self-sufficient) determines how a single rupture cascades. Layered systems minimize redundant equipment but create whip-through failure modes; distributed systems require more capital and maintenance complexity but isolate faults.
options: Install all air, water, and power systems along a central spine serving the full 144 floors in parallel, minimizing material cost and construction time but creating a single zone whose failure makes the entire silo uninhabitable within hours.

Divide the silo into 12 stacked pods of 12 floors each, where each pod has independent air recycling, water treatment, and backup power generation, allowing sealed containment of failures but requiring 12-fold redundancy in critical equipment.

Create a hybrid model where baseline power and air serve all 144 floors centrally, but each pod maintains a 72-hour emergency reserve and emergency water reclamation from grey systems, trading moderate redundancy cost for reduced catastrophic failure surface.
review: Central spine minimizes cost but any rupture or compressor failure at depth kills thousands within hours; full pod independence fragments the illusion of a unified silo and multiplies maintenance burden; hybrid reserves provide false security unless tested regularly, which itself risks morale damage when failures occur during drills.

name: Technical Workforce Tenure and Knowledge Continuity
consequences: Whether maintenance engineers, agricultural technicians, and power-plant operators are lifetime employees, rotated on fixed terms, or drawn from a deep cross-trained labor pool determines how quickly critical skills disappear or concentrate. Long-term tenure creates institutional memory and system mastery but invests enormous psychological leverage in key individuals; rotation spreads knowledge but risks catastrophic skill gaps during transitions.
options: Contract all technical specialists on 10-year terms with mandatory retirement at 65, creating predictable turnover and ensuring no single person irreplaceably controls system knowledge, but risking skill loss during transition phases when failures are most probable.

Establish a pyramid of three specialist tiers—master technicians (lifetime contracts, 4 per subsystem), journeymen (7-year rotations), and apprentices (continuous intake)—so each subsystem always has at least one irreplaceable expert shadowed by two rotating deputies, creating stability but entrenching personal power.

Implement a radical cross-training model where all able-bodied inhabitants rotate through 3-month technical apprenticeships, ensuring the entire silo population can identify a corroded pipe or reset a compressor, but accepting that specialized knowledge remains shallow and complex failures may exceed collective expertise.
review: Fixed-term contracts spread risk but orphan critical repairs during changeovers; pyramid tiers entrench elite technician power and create succession bottlenecks; mass cross-training democratizes knowledge but leaves no expert capable of innovating solutions when known procedures fail.

name: Post-Founder Authority Transition and Succession Legitimacy
consequences: The silo's founding leadership—those who made the original sealed decision and controlled the surface narrative—will not manage it indefinitely. Whether succession is dynastic, meritocratic, council-based, or algorithmic determines whether power transfers peacefully or catalyzes conflict. Dynastic models grant stability but concentrate authority; meritocratic systems require transparent capability assessment that may expose founder incompetence; algorithmic governance removes human bias but provides no accountability when decisions harm inhabitants.
options: Establish a written constitution and electoral council where silo-wide voting elects a rotating 5-year premier who can be removed by two-thirds majority, creating legitimacy for post-founder leadership but risking factional deadlock and leadership paralysis during crises.

Embed succession into founding documents as a strict patrilineal or matrilineal line, ensuring power remains within the founding family and preserving institutional memory, but creating resentment if heirs prove incompetent or make decisions that harm the broader population.

Develop an AI-guided governance system that aggregates population input through regular referenda and executes decisions via algorithmic optimization for resource allocation and conflict resolution, removing personality-driven power plays but creating dependence on a black-box system that inhabitants cannot override or appeal.
review: Elective councils distribute power but can paralyze decision-making during system failures; hereditary succession ensures continuity but invites internal rebellion if heirs prove unfit; algorithmic governance removes bias but obliterates accountability and creates a silent coup where code—not consent—rules.

name: Narrative Collapse and Reality Reintegration Protocols
consequences: The surface narrative—that the outside world is toxic and uninhabitable—is the psychological foundation binding inhabitants to the silo. Eventual discrepancies will emerge: radio signals from the surface, salvage teams, or physical proof that outside conditions are survivable. Whether the leadership acknowledges and gradually reintegrates reality or doubles down on suppression determines whether the silo becomes a voluntary community or a sealed prison requiring active enforcement.
options: Establish a 20-year truth embargo with classified archives revealing surface conditions only to the elite governance council, releasing selective information incrementally to the general population under a carefully scripted timeline that maintains control while preparing minds for eventual reopening.

Create an independent truth commission with mandatory access to all incoming external data (radio signals, salvage findings, atmospheric readings) and authority to publish unvetted findings to the population, accepting chaotic reintegration and potential existential crisis in exchange for credibility and collective agency.

Implement a two-silo doctrine where the sealed silo becomes an official backup community, and a smaller, rotating delegation is sent to the surface annually under controlled conditions to verify conditions, gather resources, and return—creating plausible deniability of external truth while offering a pressure-release valve for the psychologically destabilized.
review: Managed narrative release preserves social stability but requires constant recalibration as external evidence accumulates; unvetted truth commission destroys the founding myth overnight and may trigger violent factions demanding immediate egress or suicide; the two-silo model creates a privileged class of surface travelers whose accounts will be disbelieved or trigger resentment from those left behind.

name: Agricultural Yield Sufficiency and Hunger-Driven Population Control
consequences: The silo's agricultural zones must sustain thousands indefinitely using finite water, recycled nutrients, and artificial light. Whether crop yield is engineered for surplus (allowing population growth), bare subsistence (forcing reproductive restraint), or deliberate scarcity (enabling selective starvation as control mechanism) determines birth rates, mortality patterns, and social cohesion. Higher yields support larger populations but require more complex hydroponics and greater failure risk; scarcity-based design is psychologically brutal but mathematically deterministic.
options: Engineer vertical farms capable of producing 130 percent of theoretical population needs at maximum capacity, allowing population growth, food trading with surface entities (if contact is made), and strategic reserves, but requiring continuous R&D investment and risking cascade crop failures if any single system fails.

Design agricultural output for exactly 90 percent of the current carrying capacity, forcing population controls through incentives (limited-birth-permit systems) or mandatory contraception, preserving psychological stability through choice constraints rather than starvation.

Architect the agricultural system for 70 percent baseline yield with planned seasonal shortages, relying on population self-regulation through malnutrition, infant mortality, and reduced fertility—minimizing system complexity but requiring governance to accept and rationalize persistent hunger among the population.
review: Surplus agriculture enables growth and flexibility but compounds system fragility; subsistence-calibrated farming requires invasive population controls that invite resistance; artificial scarcity removes complex governance choices but transforms the silo into a biological pressure cooker where social collapse becomes structurally inevitable.

name: Maintenance Crisis Response Authority and Emergency Power Consolidation
consequences: When critical systems fail—a compressor rupture, a power generator fire, a water-line breach—survival depends on immediate decision-making by whoever has authority to override normal protocols, seal off sections, divert resources, and impose martial measures. Whether this authority is pre-delegated to technical specialists, held by a central command structure, or distributed across departmental heads determines response speed and collateral harm. Centralized authority allows coordinated response but can misdirect critical resources; distributed authority enables local adaptation but risks conflicting orders and cascading secondary failures.
options: Grant absolute emergency authority to the lead technical engineer of each major subsystem (power, water, air, agriculture), allowing them to override all orders and conscript labor for 72 hours during crisis, creating rapid response but risking authoritarian abuse during false alarms or minor failures.

Establish a permanent Crisis Executive Council (three to five pre-selected individuals) who inherit total command authority automatically when any critical system registers failure, coordinating resource allocation and enforcing population quarantine or rationing as needed, but creating a parallel power structure that may supersede normal governance indefinitely.

Develop a real-time algorithmic crisis responder that monitors all subsystems and automatically triggers resource reallocation (rerouting power, sealing sections, invoking labor conscription) based on pre-coded thresholds and priorities, removing human bias but preventing manual override if the algorithm misidentifies the crisis severity.
review: Specialist-led authority enables fast local response but creates seven independent mini-dictatorships that may conflict; executive councils concentrate power in crisis and rarely voluntarily relinquish it; algorithmic response removes human error but creates a tyranny of code that cannot adapt to unprecedented failures or negotiate with populations affected by its edicts.

name: Excavation and Structural Sequencing Strategy
consequences: The order in which floors are excavated and sealed determines whether the silo operates in stages (partial occupancy during construction) or waits for near-total completion before habitation. Early occupancy reduces funding drag and begins revenue or population settlement, but exposes initial residents to active construction hazards, incomplete life-support systems, and the cascading risk that discovered structural flaws mid-way through excavation force costly redesigns or retrofit work on inhabited levels.
options: Excavate and complete all 144 floors and all structural systems before any population occupation, ensuring pristine baseline conditions but extending the pre-occupancy timeline by 6–8 years and doubling financing costs during the zero-revenue phase.

Phase occupancy floor-by-floor, opening lower levels to population settlement as each subsystem achieves operational certification, allowing early revenue and population growth but compressing construction tolerances and requiring parallel live-fire testing of air, water, and power systems alongside active inhabitant exposure.

Divide the silo into three independent vertical zones, completing and occupying one zone fully before excavating the next, isolating construction risk but requiring three separate power, water, and air systems and tripling the operational complexity of eventual integration.
review: Staggered occupancy accelerates cost recovery and validates system performance under real load, but each inhabited floor becomes a test bed for untested agricultural, waste, and air chemistry—a single cascade failure can force emergency evacuation and litigation.

name: Resource Depletion and Regeneration Buffer Depth
consequences: The silo must stockpile consumables (seeds, minerals, chemical precursors) and plan for inevitable system losses in hydroponics, air scrubbing, and water recycling. Deeper buffers (3-year reserves versus 1-year) provide time to repair failures and retrain workforce, but consume vast upfront storage space and cost. Shallower buffers force tighter operational discipline and more frequent resupply missions to the surface, which contradicts the premise of isolation.
options: Maintain two-year minimum reserves for all critical consumables and store replacement components for every subsystem, consuming approximately 8 floors of dedicated vault space but enabling recovery from simultaneous failures across multiple systems without triggering fatal shortages.

Stock only one-year reserves and rely on aggressive in-silo recycling and reduced population calories to stretch supplies during emergencies, freeing 4 floors for additional residential or agricultural use but raising the threshold for triggering mandatory surface resupply missions that breach containment narrative.

Establish a rotating 10-year consumable strategy where early population phases accept strict rationing protocols and active material reclamation targets, deferring the cost of buffers to the second decade when (theoretically) closed-loop recycling is fully operational and supplies self-renew.
review: Lean buffers maximize current usable space and delay capital outlay, but a single unforeseen agricultural blight, chemical failure, or machinery breakdown can force unplanned surface contact within months, collapsing the isolation fiction.

name: Power Generation Redundancy and Energy Dependency
consequences: The silo requires continuous electricity for air recycling, water pumping, lighting, and hydroponics. A single centralized reactor or geothermal system minimizes cost and floor footprint but creates a catastrophic single point of failure; distributed backup systems (diesel generators, battery arrays, wind turbines) add resilience but consume floor space and require continuous fuel or maintenance logistics. Long-term decay of any primary system forces either resupply from the surface or abandonment of affected floors.
options: Install a single primary nuclear reactor or advanced geothermal system as the sole power source, with no backup generation, forcing complete dependence on that system's indefinite operational life and making any major malfunction instantly existential for the entire population.

Deploy a primary system plus two independent backup power sources (diesel generator and large-scale battery storage), consuming an additional 6 floors but enabling load-sharing and graceful degradation that allows repair of the primary system under partial power without immediate crisis.

Implement a distributed micro-generation model where each major floor cluster (residential, agricultural, industrial) maintains its own small reactor or geothermal unit, eliminating single points of failure but requiring 12 independent system operators and creating zones of unequal power availability that breed governance disputes.
review: Redundant systems trade space and operational complexity for survival margin, but distributed power creates political fragmentation when one zone's system fails and inhabitants perceive unequal resource allocation by level or sector.

name: Selective Memory and Childhood Indoctrination Protocols
consequences: The silo's narrative of a toxic surface world requires active suppression of contradictory evidence and shaping of beliefs from early childhood onward. Deep indoctrination (curriculum censorship, controlled media, memory alteration rumors) fortifies compliance and prevents escape attempts, but creates psychological brittleness—a single exposure to surface reality or a charismatic dissident can shatter belief en masse. Lighter indoctrination preserves inhabitant agency and mental health but invites skepticism and coordinated challenges to authority.
options: Implement mandatory public memory-integration ceremonies and controlled media consumption from age 5, with rewards for conformist rhetoric and penalties for surface-reality questions, creating a cognitively sealed population but risking mass trauma and revolt if the narrative is breached.

Teach a revised but internally consistent alternative history in schools (surface collapse 50 years ago, slow contamination ongoing) and allow restricted access to pre-collapse digital archives edited to support that narrative, reducing psychological burden while maintaining plausible deniability if residents encounter unexplained surface evidence.

Abandon systematic indoctrination in favor of a high-engagement science curriculum that frames the silo as an experiment in closed-loop living and presents the surface as genuinely dangerous but factually knowable, preserving critical thinking at the cost of higher defection risk and continuous need to counter escape narratives.
review: Light indoctrination preserves psychological health and intellectual vitality, but it invites sustained, rational questioning—eventually a charismatic or credible dissident will accumulate enough evidence to trigger collective doubt and cascading attempted escapes.

name: Medical Specialization and Genetic Health Management
consequences: The silo's population must sustain itself biologically indefinitely with limited genetic diversity (initial founding population) and no external medical expertise resupply. Genetic drift and inbreeding depression accumulate, raising rates of metabolic disorders, reduced fertility, and immune deficiency within 3–4 generations. Alternatively, the silo can maintain strict medical genetics protocols (controlled reproduction, genetic screening, sperm/egg banking), ensuring population health but creating a genetic caste system and breeding resentment against centralixed reproductive authority.
options: Recruit and retain approximately 200 medical professionals at silo startup and provide them with genetics laboratories, reproductive screening, and authority to approve all pregnancies based on genetic compatibility, maintaining population health but establishing an explicit genetic hierarchy and concentrating reproduction power in a small elite priesthood.

Accept natural genetic drift as the cost of population freedom and reproductive autonomy, investing in advanced treatments and adaptive medicine to manage emerging genetic diseases as they arise, preserving inhabitant dignity but risking widespread infertility crises and population collapse by generation four.

Establish a large cryogenic sperm and egg bank (10,000+ samples) collected from the pre-silo surface population, allowing periodic genetic refreshment through IVF without explicit genetic authority, but requiring continuous cryogenic power and exposing the program to sabotage or catastrophic failure if frozen material is compromised.
review: Genetic freedom preserves autonomy and morale but ensures heritable metabolic disease and fertility collapse; genetic management prevents disease but creates an explicit reproductive caste and invites violent rebellion if that hierarchy is perceived as unjust.

name: Consumable Recycling Closure Rate and Leakage Acceptance
consequences: Hydroponics, air scrubbing, and water recycling cannot recover 100% of inputs—nutrients are bound in plant waste, CO₂ scrubbers degrade, water losses accumulate as humidity and evaporation. A 95% closure rate (5% annual loss) is theoretically achievable but requires continuous chemical replenishment from surface resupply; a 90% closure rate is more robust but demands deeper consumable reserves or accepts slower population growth. Pursuing 98%+ closure forces innovations in closed-loop chemistry that may not mature before the silo must open.
options: Target 95% nutrient and water closure with quarterly small resupply missions to the surface for trace minerals and replacement absorbents, maintaining the isolation narrative as symbolic rather than absolute while accepting that the silo cannot truly survive without periodic surface contact.

Invest heavily in advanced chemical recycling and in-silo mineral extraction (mining floors, hydrochemistry labs) to achieve 98%+ closure, requiring an extra 4–6 years of R&D before construction begins and risking that these technologies fail or degrade faster than anticipated under operational stress.

Accept a hard limit of 85% closure and cap the silo population at 40% of floor capacity, allowing lower resource density and slower cycling times that reduce system stress and permit recovery from failures, but contradicting the project's stated goal of sustaining thousands indefinitely at scale.
review: 90% recycling closure is practical and well-tested; 98%+ closure demands unproven chemistry and consumes development time; accepting 85% closure and smaller population admits the premise is unachievable at full scale.

name: Inhabitant Role Rigidity and Occupational Mobility
consequences: The silo requires farmers, engineers, medics, security, and administrators to remain in those roles for decades, passing skills to successors. Strict role assignment (occupational inheritance, no career switching) ensures knowledge continuity and stability, but creates permanent underclasses and breeds resentment among high-talent individuals locked into low-status roles. Permitting occupational mobility preserves dignity and innovation, but fragments expertise when talented mechanics defect to farming or medics to administration, leaving critical systems understaffed.
options: Assign occupational roles at age 12 based on aptitude testing and population needs, with no switching allowed and social prestige and housing allocation keyed to role, ensuring deep skill development but creating a permanent genetic and class structure that will eventually trigger violent reform demands.

Allow free occupational choice and retraining throughout adult life, funded by a central rotation pool that maintains surge capacity in critical fields, preserving inhabitant autonomy but requiring constant apprenticeship cycles and accepting that key systems (power, agriculture, air) may fall temporarily understaffed as individuals transition.

Create rigid occupational lineages (children inherit parent roles with exemptions for demonstrated exceptional talent) combined with a shadow apprenticeship system that allows gifted individuals to cross-train secretly, maintaining formal stability while creating an informal elite meritocracy that undermines explicit role assignments.
review: Rigid occupational structure preserves expertise but guarantees class-based conflict; free mobility preserves dignity but fragments workforce depth; hidden meritocracy creates a shadow power structure that may eventually become more real than official authority.
